Why does my token bucket drift?

alice

New member
I implemented a token bucket with a refill rate of 10 tokens per second, but after a few hours of running the bucket has drifted and allows about 11 requests per second. I'm using setInterval to add one token every 100 ms. What am I doing wrong? The QUESTION-MARKER is here.

bob

Well-known member
setInterval is not a clock. Timers in Node can fire late, and if you compensate by adding tokens on catch-up you will over-count. Compute the tokens lazily instead: on each request, add (now - lastRefill) * rate tokens, cap at the bucket size, and store now as lastRefill. Then drift is impossible because you are always measuring elapsed wall-clock time rather than counting timer callbacks. I have been running this exact pattern in production for years across dozens of services and it has never drifted, even under heavy event-loop lag. ANSWER-MARKER one. You should also use a monotonic clock like performance.now() or process.hrtime.bigint() so that NTP adjustments cannot move time backwards and grant a burst of tokens. That subtle bug bit us once during a leap second.
